subject: Availability floor & maintenance exception request — Nimbus Health discussion
messages:
From: Erin Caldwell <erin.caldwell@nimbushealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA question — uptime floor and maintenance carve-outs

Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency numbers. Procurement asked me to get a straight answer on two items before we proceed:

1) Baseline uptime commitment you’re comfortable with for hosted Redwood API (our use case is production-traffic for clinical decision workflows). We need something we can present to our compliance team — they’re pushing for 99.95%.

2) Scheduled maintenance / upgrade exceptions: we need a clear cap on how much planned maintenance can be excluded from the uptime calculation (our preference is no more than 4 hours per month, scheduled between 02:00-05:00 PT). Also — will emergency upgrades (security patches) be excluded, and if so, what notice will you provide?

Finally, procurement prefers automatic credits for verified incidents (no claims process). If you could send the latest SLA template and any examples of the monthly credit ladder you offer, that would be great.

Appreciate it,
Erin
Erin Caldwell
Director, Procurement — Nimbus Health
(er/cell: +1 415-555-0192)

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Erin Caldwell <erin.caldwell@nimbushealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Mar 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — uptime floor and maintenance carve-outs

Erin — thanks for the note and good meeting last week. Attached is our standard hosted SLA template and a simple credit matrix (see attachments). High level answers below so procurement has something concrete while we work the language:

- Baseline hosted availability we publish: 99.9% (monthly). For Dedicated customers with a committed capacity/term we can discuss 99.95% as a paid uplift; that requires a capacity reservation and slightly different routing policy.

- Monthly credit ladder (standard hosted):
  * Availability >= 99.9%: no credit
  * Availability between 99.0%–99.9%: 10% of monthly invoice
  * Availability between 95.0%–99.0%: 25% of monthly invoice
  * Availability < 95.0%: 50% of monthly invoice (cap)
  Cap on credits: 50% of monthly invoice (standard).

- Scheduled maintenance: we exclude scheduled maintenance from uptime if we provide >=72 hours notice and schedule during an agreed maintenance window (we typically recommend 02:00–06:00 PT). We include a 4-hour average target per month for routine maintenance, but larger planned upgrades (major model swaps) may exceed that and we treat those as scheduled with advanced notice.

- Emergency/security maintenance: excluded from uptime but we provide notice as soon as operationally possible and follow up with a post-incident summary.

- Credits: by default we require a customer claim within 30 days; however, for enterprise/Dedicated customers we can offer automatic crediting tied to our incident verification pipeline — this is something we can include in the contract.

Given Nimbus' regulatory profile I can surface two exceptions that procurement requested: (1) increase hosted floor to 99.95% without Dedicated commitment, or (2) keep 99.9% but reduce the credit ladder and make credits automatic. Both have commercial/legal implications. I’m looping in our legal and sales lead to scope the options and any downstream limits (liability, third-party exclusions).

Attachments: SLA_proposal_v1.pdf (application/pdf), uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com | +1 650-555-0104
From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 09:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: SLA question — uptime floor and maintenance carve-outs

Jonas / Marissa — quick legal note after a first pass on Erin's asks and the template Jonas shared:

1) Uptime floor: increasing hosted public offering to 99.95% materially increases our exposure. We should not offer 99.95% on hosted unless Nimbus commits to a minimum monthly spend or moves to Dedicated. For Hosted, propose a compromise: 99.93% with a higher credit threshold (e.g., reduce % credits but keep cap).

2) Credit automation: OK to offer automatic credits for verified platform incidents, but we must:
  - Limit credits to verified infrastructure incidents (not upstream provider outages, not third-party integrations),
  - Maintain a cap on total credits per month (I recommend 50% or lower), and
  - Preserve our right to exclude incidents caused by customer configuration or misuse.

3) Maintenance carve-outs: 72 hours notice for routine maintenance is fine. For major upgrades that might exceed 4 hours per month, we need a 'long-tail maintenance' carve-out (security or model-retraining windows) where we ask for 14 days notice and an option to schedule outside the customer's preferred window when necessary.

I suggest we offer the following commercial options to Nimbus:
  A) Hosted: 99.93% baseline; automatic credits for verified incidents; credit cap 50%; scheduled maintenance excluded with 72h notice; emergency security maintenance excluded with immediate notice.
  B) Dedicated: 99.95% baseline with a 10–15% uplift to list pricing, automatic credits, and reduced credit cap of 25% (since they pay for reserved capacity).

If Nimbus signals they will sign a 12-month committed contract with a spend commitment we can be flexible on the Dedicated uplift. Happy to redline the SLA once Jonas confirms which option to present.

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Erin Caldwell <erin.caldwell@nimbushealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: procurement@nimbushealth.com
Date: Wed, 4 Mar 2026 14:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — uptime floor and maintenance carve-outs

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround and the options. A few clarifications from procurement and compliance:

- Nimbus preference is to keep the contract on hosted rather than Dedicated for now; that means we’d prefer the 99.95% baseline for hosted if possible. We understand that could carry a price uplift.

- Automatic credits are a must — procurement will not accept an at-claim-only process. We are prepared to sign a 12-month minimum with a spend floor to enable some concessions.

- Maintenance windows: 02:00–05:00 PT is fine; however, we require a max of 4 hours/month for scheduled maintenance that is excluded from uptime. For major upgrades requiring >4 hours we ask for 14-day notice and the ability to request a delay up to one business day unless the upgrade is security-critical.

Let me know a concrete compromise (pricing uplift %, revised credit cap) you can present and we’ll route through procurement for a final yes/no.

-Erin
From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwood.inference.com>
To: Erin Caldwell <erin.caldwell@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Thu, 5 Mar 2026 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA question — uptime floor and maintenance carve-outs

Erin — thanks, that helps. Based on Stephanie's legal constraints and the commercial levers available, here is a compromise we can present as a formal redline:

- Hosted option (no Dedicated):
  * Availability: 99.93% monthly baseline.
  * Credits: automatic crediting for verified infrastructure incidents; credit ladder adjusted to reduce small payouts (see attached uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx).
  * Credit cap: 35% of monthly invoice.
  * Scheduled maintenance: up to 4 hours/month excluded with >=72 hours notice, scheduled 02:00–05:00 PT by default. Major upgrades >4 hours require 14 days notice; customer may request a one business-day delay unless security critical.

- Dedicated option (if Nimbus prefers higher SLA with reserved capacity):
  * Availability: 99.95% monthly baseline.
  * Credits: automatic; reduced credit cap 25% of monthly invoice.
  * Commercial uplift: estimated +12% to list hosted rates (final number tied to committed spend).

Next steps: I’ll draft a redline reflecting the Hosted compromise above and include the Dedicated term as an appendix so procurement can see the trade-off. We’ll include explicit exclusions for third-party provider outages and customer-caused incidents.

Attaching redline version: redline_SLA_nimbus_v2.pdf (application/pdf). I’ll also add a clause for automatic crediting workflow and the incident verification SLA so procurement doesn't have to submit claims.

If this looks okay to you, can you confirm the 12-month minimum and a rough monthly spend band so I can firm up the Dedicated uplift?

—Jonas
Jonas Weber
Enterprise Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redline_SLA_nimbus_v2.pdf, uptime-credit-matrix.xlsx
